questions.stem: Which of the following data elements are key to an effective Software Asset Management practice within ServiceNow? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: An effective SAM practice requires Software Allocations (assigning rights to users/devices), Software Models (classification of acquired software), Foundation Data (accurate CMDB/CI data underpinning all SAM processes), and Software Entitlements (purchased license rights). Software contracts (D) support SAM but are not one of the four core data elements — allocations, models, foundation data, and entitlements are the primary pillars.

questions.stem:
HOTSPOT -
Match the best practice method for the amount of data:
questions.explanation: The image shows a matching exercise for SAM data population methods. Discovery is the best practice for large amounts of data — it automatically scans and populates software installations across the environment at scale. Import Data (via import sets and transform maps) is suited for medium amounts — efficient for bulk loads from spreadsheets or external tools. Manual entry through ServiceNow forms is appropriate for small amounts of data — practical for one-off entries or small data sets that don't justify automation setup.

questions.stem: Within Software Asset Management there are many key terms to understand, what is the best definition for Normalization?

options.text: One or more use rights assigned to a specific device or user
The process of standardizing discovered software installation to defined norms
The process of producing a compliance position by comparing the number of software rights acquired against the normalized software inventory
Software license details that define use rights

questions.explanation: Normalization is the process of standardizing discovered software installation data to defined norms. It maps raw discovery data (varying publisher names, product names, versions) to consistent, canonical software discovery models. Option A describes allocation, B describes classification/modeling, D describes reconciliation, and E describes entitlement attributes.

questions.stem: Which discovery sources are recommended by ServiceNow to populate ServiceNow software installation table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: ServiceNow recommends Microsoft SCCM and ServiceNow Discovery as discovery sources to populate the software installation table (cmdb_sam_sw_install). SCCM is a widely-used third-party tool with a dedicated integration plugin, and ServiceNow Discovery is the native solution. Service Mapping (A) maps business services, not software installations. HP UCMDB (B) and Orchestration (E) are not recommended discovery sources for SAM.

questions.stem: Creation of a template can help facilitate future data imports and be reused to import and transform data.
questions.explanation: Creating a template facilitates future data imports and can be reused to import and transform data. Templates in ServiceNow (import set templates, transform map templates) save field mappings and configurations so the same import structure can be applied repeatedly without reconfiguration.

questions.stem: Client access is the right to use for a specific amount of time.
questions.explanation: Client Access License (CAL) is the right for a user or device to access server software — it is not specifically about time-limited usage. A subscription license is time-based. A CAL grants access rights to a server, and is measured per user or per device, not by duration. The statement confuses CAL with subscription licensing.

questions.stem: Coalesce can only use a single field to uniquely identify a record.
questions.explanation: Coalesce can use multiple fields to uniquely identify a record during import. When multiple fields are marked as coalesce fields on a transform map, ServiceNow uses the combination of all coalesced fields to determine whether to update an existing record or create a new one. This prevents duplicate records when importing data.

questions.stem: When receiving an order, which data point is mandatory?
questions.explanation: When receiving an order (creating asset records from a purchase order), the Asset Tag is mandatory. It serves as the unique identifier for each physical or logical asset in ServiceNow. Serial Number, Assigned To, and Cost are important but not mandatory during the receiving process — Asset Tag is required to create the asset record.

questions.stem: How are the Software Asset Management Professional Plugins activated?

options.text: They are requested from and activated by an admin user
They are activated by the sam_developer user
They are activated by the sam_admin user
They are requested from and activated by ServiceNow support
They are activated by default in the base ServiceNow system

questions.explanation: SAM Professional plugins are requested from and activated by ServiceNow support (HI). They are not self-service plugins — an administrator must submit a request to ServiceNow, and ServiceNow support activates them on the instance. They are not activated by default (E), nor can sam_admin (C) or sam_developer (B) activate them directly.

questions.stem: Which of the following are true of plugins? (Choose two.)

options.text: Plugins can be disabled or deactivated when no longer in use.
Plugins can be activated by default in the base ServiceNow system.
When a plugin is active you cannot hide its functionality.
Plugins are stand-alone and do not depend on other plugins being activated.
Plugins are software components that provide specific features and functionalities.

questions.explanation: Plugins can be activated by default in the base ServiceNow system (B) — many come pre-activated. Plugins are software components that provide specific features and functionalities (E). Plugins generally cannot be disabled/deactivated once activated (A is false). Plugins can have their UI hidden (C is false). Many plugins depend on other plugins being activated first (D is false).

questions.stem: When receiving software related to a purchase order in ServiceNow, which data point is mandatory?
questions.explanation: When receiving software related to a purchase order, the Asset Tag is mandatory. It uniquely identifies the software asset record in ServiceNow. Serial Number (A) applies more to hardware, Assigned To (B) and Cost (C) are optional during receiving, and License key (D) is an attribute but not mandatory for the receiving process.

questions.stem: Which of the following are NOT features of the Publisher workbench navigation tree? (Choose two.)

options.text: List of all publishers out of compliance

questions.explanation: The Publisher workbench navigation tree does NOT include a list of all publishers (B) or a list of all publishers out of compliance (F) as tree features. The navigation tree features include expand/collapse links (A), software model compliance icons (C), filter products (D), and a compliance toggle switch (E). The publisher lists are on the main results screen, not the navigation tree.

questions.stem: Mechanism for mapping data from the import set table to the permanent table in ServiceNow is called:
questions.explanation: A Transform Map maps data from an import set table to a permanent target table in ServiceNow. It defines field mappings, coalesce rules, and transformation scripts that control how imported data is written to production tables. Mapping Assist is a feature within transform maps, not the mechanism itself.

questions.stem: In which stage of the ServiceNow Implementation Methodology (SIM) is the purpose to define processes and requirements for engagement and finalize delivery plan and user stories?
questions.explanation: In the ServiceNow Implementation Methodology (SIM), the Prepare stage defines processes and requirements for the engagement and finalizes the delivery plan and user stories. The SIM stages are: Initiate (kickoff), Prepare (define requirements/plan), Create (build/configure), Transition (UAT/go-live prep), and Close (handoff). Prepare is where detailed scoping and planning happens.

questions.stem: What is used to determine if installations are a part of a suite only when the suite parent is not discovered on a device?
questions.explanation: The inference percent is used to determine if installations are part of a suite when the suite parent is not discovered on a device. If a certain percentage of the suite's component products are found installed, the system infers the suite is present. This threshold percentage controls how aggressively suite membership is inferred from partial component discovery.

questions.stem: Which statements are true in regards to ServiceNow’s Client Software Distribution (CSD) functionality? (Choose two.)

options.text: Removes software daily utilizing a scheduled job.
ServiceNow does not have Client Software Distribution.
The first stage in the CSD process flow is configuration.
CSD can automatically distribute and reclaim software without a license for Orchestration.

questions.explanation: CSD removes software daily utilizing a scheduled job (A) and the first stage in the CSD process flow is configuration (C). CSD is a real feature in ServiceNow that integrates with Orchestration to automatically install and uninstall software. Option B is false — ServiceNow does have CSD. Option D is false — CSD requires a separate Orchestration license.

questions.stem: Which of the following SAM roles has permission to grant a user the script writing capability?
questions.explanation: The sam_developer role has permission to grant script writing capability in SAM. This role is specifically designed for users who need to create and modify custom license scripts and other scripted components within SAM. The sam_admin can read but not create custom scripts, while sam_user and asset roles have more limited permissions.

questions.stem: Within the Capability Blueprint there are 4 tiers identified. Which tier is identified as Tier 1?
questions.explanation: In the SAM Capability Blueprint, Tier 1 is Trustworthy Data — 'Know what you have so you can manage it.' The four tiers in order are: Tier 1 = Trustworthy Data, Tier 2 = Practical Management, Tier 3 = Operational Integration, Tier 4 = Strategic Conformance. You must first establish reliable data before managing, integrating, or optimizing.

questions.stem: Which of the following are available publisher packs? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The available publisher packs in ServiceNow SAM are SAP (A), Citrix (C), Oracle (E), and IBM (F). Additionally Microsoft and VMware are available. OpenVMS (B) and NetSuite (D) are not available as publisher packs. Publisher packs extend SAM functionality with publisher-specific license metric calculations and reconciliation rules.

questions.stem: Which of the following features aggregates usage over a period of time and specifies a minimum number of hours the software must be used, or date last used?
questions.explanation: Software reclamation rules aggregate usage over a period of time and specify minimum hours required or date last used thresholds. Reclamation rules identify software installations with low or no usage that can be reclaimed. Software usage metering (A) collects raw usage data. Reclamation types (C) define categories. Reclamation rules use those usage records to flag candidates for license recovery.

questions.stem: By default, which user role must verify the successful activation of plugins by ServiceNow support?
questions.explanation: The sam_admin role is responsible for verifying the successful activation of SAM plugins by ServiceNow support. After requesting plugin activation from ServiceNow, the SAM administrator verifies that the plugins are active and functioning correctly. While sys_admin (D) can also verify, sam_admin is the default persona responsible for SAM plugin management.

questions.stem: When populating software usage records automatically via Microsoft System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM), which plugins are required? (Choose two.)

options.text: Performance Analytics Premium for Software Asset Management plugin

questions.explanation: To populate software usage records automatically via Microsoft SCCM, you need the Microsoft SCCM Software Usage plugin (B) and the Microsoft SCCM Integration plugin (C). The SCCM Integration plugin provides the base connectivity to SCCM, while the SCCM Software Usage plugin specifically handles importing usage data. The Microsoft Publisher Pack (A) is for license metrics, not usage import.

questions.stem: An allocation is automatically created in which of the following scenarios? (Choose two.)

options.text: After receiving the rights for software from a purchase order
After a Create allocation remediation option has been taken
After reconciliation runs and identifies that rights are ‘Not allocated in use’
When a software installation is discovered
After successfully sourcing a request via an existing entitlement

questions.explanation: An allocation is automatically created after a Create Allocation remediation option has been taken (B) and after successfully sourcing a request via an existing entitlement (E). Receiving rights from a PO (A) creates entitlements, not allocations automatically. Reconciliation (C) identifies compliance gaps but doesn't auto-create allocations. Discovery (D) creates installation records, not allocations.

questions.stem: In the ServiceNow base platform, which roles have the ability to refresh processor definitions?
questions.explanation: The sam_admin and sys_admin roles have the ability to refresh processor definitions in the ServiceNow base platform. The sam_user role does not have this administrative capability. Refreshing processor definitions is an administrative task that recalculates normalization and content service processors.

questions.stem: Which of the following are required to import usage data using the System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM) data? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: To import usage data using SCCM, you need: Software Product (B) to associate usage with the correct product, Product Process (E) to define how SCCM data is processed and mapped, and Reclamation Rule (F) to define criteria for identifying reclamation candidates from usage data. Reclamation Candidate (A) is an output, not a requirement. Software Models (D) and SCCM Application (C) are related but not the required import elements.

questions.stem: Software usage data can be imported utilizing:
questions.explanation: In the baseline SAM Professional configuration, software usage data can be imported utilizing System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM). SCCM is the primary supported method for automated usage data import in SAM Professional. While other third-party sources (B) may work, SCCM is the built-in, recommended method with dedicated plugins. Transform Maps (A) and manual entry (D) are general import methods, not specific to usage data.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is incorrect with regards to on-premise import and export of Content Service data?

options.text: Clicking on the “Manage Software Library” module takes the user to an interceptor page where they can select to import or export data.
On-premise instances do not receive automatic Software Library updates.
Normalization content is eligible for the export feature.
By default, you are opted in to the Manage On-Premise Library (com.sn_samp_on_prem) plugin.
You must opt-in to the SAM Content Service through the Content Service setup page.

questions.explanation: The incorrect statement is that by default you are opted in to the Manage On-Premise Library plugin (D). You must opt-in manually — it is not enabled by default. The other statements are correct: the Manage Software Library module leads to an import/export interceptor (A), on-premise instances don't get automatic updates (B), normalization content is eligible for export (C), and you must opt-in through the Content Service setup page (E).

questions.stem: If a value from an import does not exist in ServiceNow and the import should not create a new record, which option should be selected?
questions.explanation: When a value from an import does not exist in ServiceNow and the import should NOT create a new record, select Reject. This prevents the import row from creating new records and marks it as rejected. Ignore would skip the field but still process the row. Create would generate a new record. Reject specifically blocks the entire row from being processed.

questions.stem: When loading a medium amount of data, which is the best method to use?

options.text: Use Discovery to find software on the network

questions.explanation: When loading a medium amount of data into ServiceNow SAM, the best method is to Import Data (import sets). Manual entry via forms is suitable for small amounts, Discovery is best for large-scale ongoing collection from the network, and import sets provide the right balance for medium volumes. Import sets allow CSV/Excel uploads with transform maps to map external data to ServiceNow tables.

questions.stem: What is a first key step prior to uploading your entitlement import data via the ServiceNow-provided template?

options.text: Ensure you have filled out every field in the template file
Ensure the entitlement data is listed on the first tab of the template file
Ensure you have downloaded and used the latest version of the template file
Ensure you have the sam_user role assigned to you

questions.explanation: The first key step before uploading entitlement import data is to ensure you have downloaded and used the latest version of the template file. ServiceNow updates templates to match current field requirements and data structures. Using an outdated template could cause import errors or missing fields. Not every field needs to be filled (A), the tab location is not the key concern (B), and sam_user may not be the required role (D).

questions.stem: What are three ways to get software asset data into ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: The three ways to get software asset data into ServiceNow are Discovery (automated scanning), Import Data (via import sets and transform maps), and Manual entry (through ServiceNow forms). These map to large/medium/small data volumes respectively. Clone (A/B) and Background Script (A/D) are not standard data input methods for SAM.

questions.stem: The Software Asset Management Content Service is automatically enabled and cannot be opted out.
questions.explanation: The SAM Content Service is NOT automatically enabled and cannot be opted out — this statement is false. The Content Service must be explicitly enabled/opted into through the Content Service setup page. Once enabled, it downloads normalization content, publisher part numbers, and lifecycle data from ServiceNow's cloud-hosted library.

questions.stem: What table is populated with the content library data that is pulled from the content service?
questions.explanation: The samp_sw_package table is populated with the content library data pulled from the Content Service. This table stores software package definitions including publisher, product, version, and edition information that is used for normalization. The cmdb_sw_product_model (B) contains software models, not raw library content.

questions.stem: When specified during an entitlement import, which of the following is matched to data in the Content Service Library and used to create a software model automatically?
questions.explanation: The Publisher Part Number (PPN) is matched to data in the Content Service Library and used to create a software model automatically during entitlement import. PPNs uniquely identify publisher-specific software products and map directly to content library entries, enabling automatic software model creation without manual configuration.

questions.stem: As part of the software normalization process, software discovery models are normalized via which mechanisms? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Software discovery models are normalized via a Scheduled Job (B) that runs daily to process discovery models through the normalization engine, and a Business Rule (C) that triggers normalization when new discovery models are created or updated. Fix scripts (A) are for one-time operations, not ongoing normalization. Integration (D) and Workflow (E) are not the normalization mechanisms.

questions.stem: What is the definition of Partially Normalized?

options.text: A discovery model normalized based on publisher field alone.
The software discovery model has not yet completed its run through the normalization process.
A discovery model was normalized based on publisher and product fields only.
A discovery model was normalized based on publisher, product, version fields.

questions.explanation: Partially Normalized means a discovery model was normalized based on publisher and product fields only, but NOT the version or edition. Full normalization includes publisher, product, version, and edition. When only publisher and product can be matched to content library entries, the status is set to Partially Normalized, indicating more data or content updates are needed for complete normalization.

questions.stem: What is the name of the Scheduled job that runs daily for normalization?
questions.explanation: The scheduled job that runs daily for normalization is Discovery Model Normalization. This job processes software discovery models through the normalization engine, matching them against the content library to standardize publisher, product, version, and edition values. Software Installation Normalization (B) and Software Model Cleanup (C) are different jobs.

questions.stem: Within Software Asset Management there are many key terms to understand, what is the best definition for Software Allocation?

options.text: One or more use rights assigned to a specific device or user.
The process of normalizing a discovered software installation to standardized values.
Finding and recognizing software or a software feature on a device.

questions.explanation: A Software Allocation is one or more use rights assigned to a specific device or user. Allocations connect entitlements (purchased rights) to the actual users or devices that consume those rights. Option B describes an entitlement (something acquired with rights), C describes normalization, and D describes discovery.

questions.stem: How often is the scheduled job for the normalization process run?

options.text: Nightly for new discovery models and weekly for all discovery models that do not have a status of normalized or manually normalized
Immediately for new discovery models and nightly for all discovery models that do not have a status of normalized or manually normalized

questions.explanation: The normalization scheduled job runs nightly (daily) by default. Each night it processes software discovery models that need normalization against the content library. While there are different aspects to normalization timing, the primary scheduled job runs on a nightly/daily schedule to process new and unresolved discovery models.

questions.stem: Discovery models may not be fully normalized until updated content is downloaded from the ServiceNow Software Content Library. How do you determine if the content has been downloaded?

options.text: Review the Last updated date of the Central Data Service Download Status jobs on the Normalization and Content Service dashboard.
Determine if the business rule “Create a Software Normalization Download” has been triggered yet or not.
Query the scheduled job reports to determine if the “Software Content Library Download” (samp_cds_download) job has completed yet.
Review the number of records in the samp_product_map table. If there are ~7,700 records in the table, the download has completed at least once.

questions.explanation: To determine if content has been downloaded from the Software Content Library, review the Last Updated date of the Central Data Service Download Status jobs on the Normalization and Content Service dashboard. This dashboard shows the status and timestamps of content downloads, making it the most reliable way to verify content availability.

questions.stem: When populating the Downgrade Rights table, if there is no software model corresponding to a discovery map, which of the following is automatically created?
questions.explanation: When populating the Downgrade Rights table, if there is no software model corresponding to a discovery map, a Software Model is automatically created. This ensures downgrade rights can be properly linked even when the target version doesn't yet have a model defined. The system auto-generates the necessary software model to maintain referential integrity.

questions.stem: For software asset management, when software is discovered, the records from the discovered pattern are copied into which table?
questions.explanation: When software is discovered, the records from discovery patterns are copied into the cmdb_sam_sw_install table (Software Installation table, though the option shows a typo). This is the core SAM table for tracking installed software across managed devices. Discovery creates installation records here that link to discovery models for normalization and reconciliation.

questions.stem: Within ServiceNow Discovery, the Exploration phase determines what?

options.text: Are you there? How will I classify you?
What else can you tell me about yourself?
How should I classify you specifically?

questions.explanation: The Exploration phase of ServiceNow Discovery determines 'What else can you tell me about yourself?' During Exploration, the system gathers detailed information about the device including installed software, running processes, network connections, and hardware specs. The four phases in order are: Scanning ('Are you there?'), Classification ('How should I classify you?'), Identification ('Have I seen you before?'), Exploration ('What else?').

questions.stem: If your organization is currently running Discovery, but has not yet installed the SAM Professional application, what must you do after installing SAM in order to make your discovered software installation information available to SAM?

options.text: Convert the records from the [cmdb_ci_spkg] table into the [cmdb_sam_sw_install] table
Run the “Migrate software installations” script to copy records from the [cmdb_ci_spkg] table to the [cmdb_sam_sw_install] table
Run the “Discover software installations” script to copy records from the [cmdb_ci_spkg] table to the [cmdb_sam_sw_install] table
Export the records from the [cmdb_ci_spkg] table into an xml spreadsheet and import them into the [cmdb_sam_sw_install] table

questions.explanation: After installing SAM Professional on an instance already running Discovery, you must run the 'Migrate software installations' script to copy records from cmdb_ci_spkg (legacy software package table) to cmdb_sam_sw_install (SAM software installation table). SAM Professional uses its own installation table, so existing discovery data must be migrated to be visible in SAM.

questions.stem: ServiceNow Discovery identifies the software running on an IP-enabled device during which of its phases?
questions.explanation: ServiceNow Discovery identifies the software running on an IP-enabled device during the Exploration phase. Exploration is the fourth and final phase where detailed information including installed software, running processes, and configuration data is gathered. Scanning detects the device, Classification determines its type, and Identification checks for existing CI records.

questions.stem: When a Software Installation record is created, ServiceNow attempts to match the installation to a:
questions.explanation: When a Software Installation record is created, ServiceNow attempts to match it to a Software Discovery Model. The discovery model represents the raw, unnormalized software identification (publisher, product, version as discovered). If a matching discovery model exists, the installation references it; if not, a new discovery model is created. The discovery model is then normalized to a software model.

questions.stem:
ServiceNow Discovery has 4 phases: Scanning; Classification; Identification; and Exploration.
In which phase is the software running on a device identified?
questions.explanation: Software running on a device is identified during the Exploration phase of Discovery. This is the same concept as Q45 — Exploration gathers detailed device information including all installed software. Scanning finds the device, Classification determines its type, Identification checks for existing records, and Exploration collects detailed data.

questions.stem: Any product that accurately discovers software installations on computers in an environment can be used as the source for a Software Installation data.
questions.explanation: This is false because ServiceNow has specific requirements for discovery data sources. Not any arbitrary product will work — the data must conform to ServiceNow's expected format and schema for the software installation table. ServiceNow specifically recommends its own Discovery and SCCM as supported sources, with dedicated integration plugins. Other tools may work with custom import sets but are not automatically compatible.

questions.stem: When are discovery models created?

options.text: They are automatically created during discovery
They are automatically created during reconciliation
They are automatically created during normalization.

questions.explanation: Discovery models are automatically created during discovery. When Discovery identifies software on a device and creates a software installation record, it also automatically creates or references a Software Discovery Model to represent the raw discovery data (publisher, product, version). They are not manually created, nor created during normalization or reconciliation (those processes consume discovery models).

questions.stem: By default, which persona is responsible for controlling the day-to-day activities of the SAM process and ensuring the overall quality of software asset data?
questions.explanation: The SAM manager is responsible for controlling day-to-day activities of the SAM process and ensuring overall quality of software asset data. The SAM manager oversees reconciliation results, allocation decisions, compliance monitoring, and reclamation processes. The SAM process owner (D) focuses on strategy and governance, while the ServiceNow administrator (A) handles technical platform tasks.

questions.stem: When creating custom products: (Choose the best answer.)

options.text: Custom products should not be tracked in ServiceNow.
Custom products should not be created for anything included in the content library.
Custom products are automatically created in the content library.
Custom products should be created for anything included in the content library.

questions.explanation: Custom products should not be created for anything included in the content library. If a product already exists in the ServiceNow Content Service library, creating a custom duplicate would cause normalization conflicts and reconciliation errors. Custom products should only be created for internally-developed or niche software not covered by the content library.

questions.stem: If a customer does not like the way reconciliation runs or calculates compliance, it is okay to modify the scripts includes, business rules and other logic to accommodate the business requirement.
questions.explanation: It is NOT okay to modify the script includes, business rules, and other out-of-box reconciliation logic to accommodate business requirements. Modifying OOB reconciliation code is unsupported and will break during upgrades. Instead, use custom license metrics, custom scripts within the SAM framework, or configuration options to tailor reconciliation behavior without altering base code.

questions.stem: By default, which ServiceNow role can view reconciliation results?
questions.explanation: The sam_user role can view reconciliation results by default. sam_user provides read access to SAM data including reconciliation product results, model results, and license metric results. The sam_admin role can both view and take action on results. There is no OOB sam_reconcile_user (A), sam_viewer (C), or sam_cmdb_user (D) role.

questions.stem: The process of determining compliance by comparing software rights owned with normalized software installations discovered is __________________ .
questions.explanation: Reconciliation is the process of determining compliance by comparing software rights owned (entitlements) with normalized software installations discovered. It produces a compliance position showing whether the organization is over-licensed, under-licensed, or compliant for each software product. Discovery (A) finds software, Allocation (B) assigns rights, Normalization (C) standardizes data.

questions.stem: The definition for _________________ in the Reconciliation Product result is: “Estimated cost of remediating non-compliance based on the least number of rights needed.”
questions.explanation: True-up cost is defined as the estimated cost of remediating non-compliance based on the least number of rights needed. When reconciliation shows fewer entitlements than installations, true-up cost calculates what would need to be purchased to become compliant. True-down cost (C) relates to over-licensing savings, and over-licensed cost (D) shows excess spending.

questions.stem: When reconciliation is run, a list of product results displays the compliance status of software versions and editions with respect to discovery and entitlements.
questions.explanation: This statement is false. Product results display compliance at the product level, aggregating all versions and editions of a product. It is the Software Model results that show compliance for specific versions and editions. Product results show an overall compliance position for the entire product across all its models and installations.

questions.stem: In order to write to the reconciliation results, a user would need the following role in ServiceNow: sam_reconcile_user
questions.explanation: This is false. There is no sam_reconcile_user role in the baseline SAM configuration. To write to reconciliation results (run reconciliation, take remediation actions), you need the sam_admin role. The sam_user role can only view reconciliation results. The question references a non-existent role.

questions.stem: Select the field attribute that indicates whether this product result is from the most recent reconciliation run.
questions.explanation: The Latest field attribute indicates whether a product result is from the most recent reconciliation run. When reconciliation runs, it generates new result records and marks them as Latest=true, while previous results are marked Latest=false. This allows filtering to see only current compliance data while preserving history.

questions.stem: In defining a Custom License Metric, in the Reconciliation Order field, the ___________ ‘metric rank priority’ number takes precedence.
questions.explanation: In defining a Custom License Metric, the lower 'metric rank priority' number takes precedence in the Reconciliation Order field. This follows standard ServiceNow priority ordering where 1 is highest priority. When multiple license metrics apply to the same product, the metric with the lowest reconciliation order number is evaluated first.

questions.stem: The license metric attributes related list contains metric values set in software entitlements, and is used for reconciliation (metric group, license metric, and software model combination).
questions.explanation: True — the license metric attributes related list contains metric values set in software entitlements and is used for reconciliation. It stores the combination of metric group, license metric, and software model that determines how entitlements are counted during the reconciliation process. These attributes define the specific rights calculation method.

questions.stem: By default, when is a product result generated for a licensable product after reconciliation?

options.text: Always, even if there are no software models defined for the product
Only when there are software entitlements defined for the product
Whenever there is at least one software model defined for the product
Only when related entitlements have a cost identified

questions.explanation: By default, a product result is always generated for a licensable product after reconciliation, even if there are no software models defined. This ensures visibility into all licensable products in the environment, including those that may have installations but no entitlements. This comprehensive approach helps identify unlicensed software.

questions.stem: Which feature provides detailed, actionable information for software reconciliation?
questions.explanation: The License Workbench provides detailed, actionable information for software reconciliation. It presents reconciliation results in a hierarchical view (publisher → product → model → license metric) with drill-down capability, remediation options, and compliance indicators. The License Position Report (B) is a static report, while the License Workbench is the interactive tool.

questions.stem: What are the four tiers of software reconciliation results? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The four tiers of software reconciliation results are: Software Publisher (E) → Software Product (B) → Software Model (F) → Software License Metric (A). Results cascade from publisher level down to license metric level, each providing increasingly granular compliance data. Entitlements (D) and Allocations (C) are inputs to reconciliation, not result tiers.

questions.stem: When reconciliation is run, what information does the license metric results display?

options.text: Results for all models and installations associated to the product
Results for all products and installations associated to the publisher
Results for each license metric associated to the software model
Results for all license metrics related to the software model

questions.explanation: License metric results display results for each license metric associated to the software model. This is the most granular tier of reconciliation results, showing compliance for specific metrics (e.g., Per Named User, Per Device) within a software model. Publisher results (B) aggregate across products, product results (A/C) aggregate across models.

questions.stem: To run an on-demand reconciliation, which module would you navigate to?

options.text: Software Asset > Reconciliation > Run License Position Report
Software Asset > Discovery > Run License Position Report

questions.explanation: To run on-demand reconciliation, navigate to Software Asset > Reconciliation > Run Reconciliation. This module allows the sam_admin to manually trigger reconciliation for all publishers or a specific publisher, rather than waiting for the weekly scheduled run.

questions.stem: Which of the following features are available from the main publisher results screen of the License Workbench? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The License Workbench main publisher results screen has three tabs: All Publishers (A), Pinned Publishers (C), and Publishers Out of Compliance (E). These tabs let users view all publishers, quickly access frequently-reviewed publishers, and focus on non-compliant publishers. Publisher Compliance (B), Publisher License Metrics (D), and Publisher Software Models (F) are not main screen tabs.

questions.stem: Which related list is NOT available from the software model on the License Workbench?
questions.explanation: Unlicensed Software Products (B) is NOT a related list on the software model in the License Workbench. The available related lists include: Unlicensed Subscriptions (A), Removal Candidates (C), Remediation Options (D), and License Metric Results (E). Unlicensed products would appear at the product result level, not at the software model level.

questions.stem: License metrics can be defined for which of the following? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: License metrics can be defined for Users (B), Cores (C), Devices (D), and Processors (G). These represent the four main measurement units for software licensing: per-user licensing, per-core licensing (common for server software), per-device licensing, and per-processor licensing. Publishers (A), Metric Types (E), and Operating Systems (F) are not license metric targets.

questions.stem: Which license metric would be used for software that is only allowed to be installed on one computer per license right?
questions.explanation: Per Named Device licenses software to be installed on one specific computer per license right. 'Named' means the license is tied to a specific, identified device. Per Processor (A) and Per Core (D) license server hardware. Per Named User (C) ties a license to a specific user, not a device.

questions.stem: Which of the following license metrics require allocations in order to maintain compliance? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Per Named Device (C) and Per Named User (D) license metrics require allocations to maintain compliance. Because 'Named' metrics tie rights to specific identified devices or users, explicit allocations are needed to track which device or user holds each right. Non-named metrics like Per Core (A), Per User (B), and Per Application Instance (F) calculate compliance from installations/entitlements without individual allocations.

questions.stem: Which of the following are NOT tabs available on the License Workbench? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Publisher License Metrics (A), Publisher Software Models (D), and Publisher Compliance (E) are NOT tabs on the License Workbench. The three actual tabs are: All Publishers (B), Publishers Out of Compliance (C), and Pinned Publishers (F). The License Workbench organizes publishers into these three views for efficient compliance management.

questions.stem: You can view IBM, Microsoft, Oracle and VMware license metrics as part of ServiceNow standard baseline configuration features.
questions.explanation: You cannot view IBM, Microsoft, Oracle, and VMware license metrics as part of standard baseline configuration. These publisher-specific metrics require separate publisher packs to be activated. Publisher packs extend SAM with vendor-specific licensing rules and are not included in the base SAM Professional installation.

questions.stem: When creating a reportable bar graph view of License Metrics, you can use which of the following options to refine how you view license metric data?
questions.explanation: When creating a reportable bar graph view of License Metrics, you can use both 'Group by' AND 'Stacked by' options to refine how you view the data. 'Group by' organizes bars by a field, and 'Stacked by' subdivides each bar by another field. Using both together provides multi-dimensional visualization of license metrics.

questions.stem: A Software Product can only have a single license metric type associated to it.
questions.explanation: A Software Product can have multiple license metric types. Different entitlements for the same product may use different metrics (e.g., Per Named User for some licenses and Per Device for others). The reconciliation engine processes each metric separately at the license metric results tier, allowing mixed metric types per product.

questions.stem: By default, the license metric field is displayed on which record form within ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: The license metric field is displayed by default on the Software Entitlement record form. Each entitlement specifies which license metric applies to the purchased rights (e.g., Per Named User, Per Device, Per Core). This determines how reconciliation counts and compares rights against installations for that entitlement.

questions.stem: What product must you procure a separate license for in order to utilize Workflow and Client Software Distribution (CSD) to automatically install software on devices.
questions.explanation: Orchestration requires a separate license to utilize Workflow and Client Software Distribution (CSD) for automatically installing software on devices. CSD leverages Orchestration's ability to execute commands on managed devices through the MID Server. Discovery (D) finds devices but doesn't install software.

questions.stem: Software license management (SLM) is a key component of the software asset lifecycle. What is its primary objective?

options.text: To convert regular per user licenses into subscription licenses
To track, control, and reduce software costs, including costs associated with non-compliance findings during a software audit
To reserve a block of licenses for a specific group of users and/or user role(s)
To accurately calculate annual true-up cost and total spend on a product
To automatically install and remove software on devices using Workflow and Client Software Distribution (CSD)

questions.explanation: Software license management's primary objective is to track, control, and reduce software costs, including costs associated with non-compliance findings during a software audit. SLM encompasses the full financial and compliance lifecycle of software assets. The other options describe specific sub-tasks or adjacent features, not the primary overall objective.

questions.stem: The Per Named Device license metric licenses which of the following?

options.text: A user for a number of installations of software
A device for a number of installations of software
A specific user for a number of installations of software
Cores on a physical server or virtual machine
A specific device for a number of installations of software

questions.explanation: Per Named Device licenses a specific device for a number of installations of software. The key word is 'specific' — Named Device means the license is tied to an identified, specific device (by name or serial number), not just any device. Option B describes a general per-device metric without the 'named' specificity.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the Metric Group on the Software Entitlement record?

options.text: To select the group of license metrics to be used on the entitlement
To select a group to see specific license metrics for a software category
To select a category of specific license entitlement attributes
To select a group to see specific license key attributes

questions.explanation: The Metric Group on the Software Entitlement record selects the group of license metrics to be used on the entitlement. Metric groups bundle related license metrics together (e.g., a Microsoft metric group containing Per Device, Per User, Per Core metrics). The entitlement references a metric group to determine which calculation method applies during reconciliation.

questions.stem: ServiceNow Performance Analytics identifies a trend that use of a certain software package has reduced over time. This is a potential indicator of what?

options.text: Your company is under-licensed for the product.
Your company needs to renegotiate your contract to get better pricing.
Your company is over-licensed for the product.
Your company needs to retire the unused entitlements.

questions.explanation: A Performance Analytics trend showing reduced usage of a software package over time is a potential indicator that the company is over-licensed for the product. If usage is declining, the organization may have more licenses than needed, representing unnecessary costs. This insight enables the SAM team to reclaim or not renew excess licenses.

questions.stem: A(n) ______________ is required for a user or device to consume software rights.
questions.explanation: An Entitlement is required for a user or device to consume software rights. Entitlements represent the purchased software rights/licenses. Without an entitlement, there are no rights to consume. Allocations (B) assign specific entitlement rights to users/devices, but the entitlement must exist first as the source of rights.

questions.stem: Which of the following is required to identify users and devices that have the right to use software?
questions.explanation: Software Allocations are required to identify which specific users and devices have the right to use software. Allocations link entitlement rights to individual users or devices. While entitlements (D) hold the purchased rights, allocations are what specifically identify WHO or WHAT has been granted those rights.

questions.stem: Which of the following allocation types are available on an entitlement record in the ServiceNow baseline configuration? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The baseline allocation types available on an entitlement record are Device allocations (A) and User allocations (E). These are the two fundamental ways to assign software rights: to specific devices or to specific users. Country (B), Company (C), and Department (D) allocations are not available in the baseline configuration.

questions.stem: When importing entitlements, a record generates the error, “Publisher Part Number not found”. However, the record is for an expired entitlement that is no longer needed. Which is the best UI action to select?
questions.explanation: For an expired entitlement that is no longer needed and generates a 'Publisher Part Number not found' error, the best action is Delete (B). Since the entitlement is expired and unneeded, deleting the import error record removes it from the queue without creating unnecessary records. Create Entitlement (A) would create an unwanted record, Create Part Number (C) would add unnecessary data, and Reject (D) marks it as an error rather than eliminating it.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes Practical Management within the capability blueprint?

options.text: Improve management controls and drive immediate benefits.
Know what you have so you can manage it.
Improve efficiency and effectiveness through integration with other areas, such as request, procurement, and IT Service Management.

questions.explanation: Practical Management (Tier 2) in the SAM Capability Blueprint is: 'Improve management controls and drive immediate benefits.' The tiers are: Tier 1 Trustworthy Data = 'Know what you have' (B), Tier 2 Practical Management = 'Improve controls' (A), Tier 3 Operational Integration = 'Integrate with other areas' (C), Tier 4 Strategic Conformance = 'Achieve best in class' (D).

questions.stem:
HOTSPOT -
Match the type of result levels with the corresponding definition.
questions.explanation: This is a HOTSPOT matching question about SAM normalization result levels. SAM normalization uses result levels to categorize how well discovered software matches the normalization library: Level 1 indicates an exact match with high confidence, Level 2 indicates a partial or close match requiring review, and Level 3 indicates no match was found requiring manual normalization. Without the exhibit, exact matching cannot be confirmed.

questions.stem: Blacklisted candidates are ______________ .

options.text: Software installations that are not normalized
Software installations not allowed in the network environment

questions.explanation: Blacklisted candidates are software installations that are not allowed in the network environment. Organizations define software blacklists for security, compliance, or policy reasons (e.g., unapproved peer-to-peer software, insecure applications). SAM tracks these installations as blacklisted candidates for removal action.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a core Software Asset Management function?
questions.explanation: Financial Management is not a core Software Asset Management function. The core SAM functions are Inventory Management (tracking what's installed), Rights Allocation (assigning licenses), and Reclamation (recovering unused licenses), along with Normalization, Reconciliation, and Compliance. While SAM handles software costs, broad Financial Management is a separate ITFM discipline.

questions.stem: In addition to creating a new purchase order for software licenses, additional remediation options are available in Software Model results to: (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: In addition to creating a new purchase order, the remediation options available in Software Model results include Remove Unallocated Installs (A) and Remove Unlicensed Installs (C). These options help achieve compliance by removing software that either has no allocation or no license. Remove Duplicate Allocations (B) and Remove Blacklisted Installs (D) are not standard remediation options at this level.

questions.stem: What list can include manual creation, remediation options, and reclamation rules?
questions.explanation: Removal Candidates is the list that can include entries from manual creation, remediation options, and reclamation rules. Removal candidates are software installations flagged for uninstallation/removal. They can be added manually by an administrator, generated from remediation actions on the License Workbench, or identified automatically through reclamation rules based on usage data.

questions.stem: Which of the following remediation options can be performed on an individual user or device basis? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Remediation options that can be performed on an individual user or device basis include Remove Unlicensed Installs (B), Create Allocations (C), and Purchase Rights (E). Remove Unallocated Installs (A) operates at the model level rather than per user/device. Remove Allocations (D) also operates at the allocation level. B, C, and E target specific users or devices.

questions.stem: Which of the following reasons could apply when a remediation option has an ‘In Progress’ status? (Choose two.)

options.text: Workflow(s) or process(es) have been initiated to allocate software rights
Rights are now available and can be consumed during reconciliation
Workflow(s) or process(es) have been initiated to purchase software rights
Workflow(s) or process(es) have been initiated to harvest software rights
Customer instance is pending updates to CDS Server

questions.explanation: A remediation option has 'In Progress' status when workflows or processes have been initiated to allocate software rights (A) or to purchase software rights (C). Both allocation and purchasing processes involve multi-step workflows (approvals, fulfillment) that take time to complete, keeping the remediation in progress until the workflow finishes.

questions.stem:
Which stage of the software asset lifecycle includes all of the following steps?
Discovering software in the environment
Normalizing installed software to standards
Reconciling entitlements to discovered software
Remediating detected variances
questions.explanation: The Manage stage of the software asset lifecycle includes discovering software, normalizing installations, reconciling entitlements to discoveries, and remediating variances. Manage is the ongoing operational phase where SAM processes run continuously. Source (D) is about procurement, Plan (E) is strategy, Support (C) is maintenance, and Sunset (A) is retirement.

questions.stem: Which catalog provides a listing of goods offered or available by a third party?
questions.explanation: The Vendor Catalog provides a listing of goods offered or available by a third party (vendor). It contains the vendor's available products and offerings. The Service Catalog (A) is for internal service requests, the Product Catalog (E) is the internal catalog of known products, and the Model Catalog (B) contains defined software/hardware models.

questions.stem: A software model can have up to how many catalog items?
questions.explanation: A software model can have up to 1 catalog item. Each software model maps to a single catalog item in the Service Catalog for requesting that specific software. This one-to-one relationship ensures clear traceability between catalog requests and the software model being provisioned.

questions.stem:
HOTSPOT -
Define the three catalogs that support the request and procurement process.
questions.explanation: The three catalogs supporting the request and procurement process are: Service Catalog (end users request software through catalog items), Product Catalog (internal listing of known/approved software products), and Vendor Catalog (third-party vendor offerings for purchasing). Together they cover the full request-to-procurement lifecycle.

questions.stem: If a user requests three items from the software catalog at the same time, how many individual requests are created?
questions.explanation: When a user requests three items from the software catalog at the same time, 1 request is created. ServiceNow creates a single Request (REQ) record that contains multiple Requested Items (RITMs), one for each catalog item. The request serves as a container for all items ordered in one submission.

questions.stem: Which of the following elements are included in Operational Integration of a SAM practice? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Operational Integration (Tier 3 of SAM Capability Blueprint) includes Software License Contracts (B), Software Sourcing (C), and License Change Projection (D). This tier focuses on integrating SAM with procurement, ITSM, and contract management processes. Entitlements (E), Allocations (F), and Retirement (A) are part of other tiers, and Model Lifecycle (G) is strategic.

questions.stem: You have a contract that is getting ready to expire. What options do you have for handling this contract and remaining compliant? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: For a contract getting ready to expire, the options to remain compliant are: Extend (B) the existing contract, Cancel (C) if the software is no longer needed, or Renew (F) with a new term. Reject (A) is not a contract action, Activate (D) is for new contracts, and Delete (E) would lose audit history.

questions.stem: The baseline sam_admin role contains the additional roles of: sam_user, asset, and procurement_user, and which of the following? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The baseline sam_admin role contains sam_user, asset, procurement_user, plus contract_manager (C) and model_manager (D). The sam_admin needs contract management access to manage software agreements and model management to define and maintain software models. itil (A) and sam_developer (B) are separate roles not inherited by sam_admin by default.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of an external audit?

options.text: To ensure your users are not running any blacklisted software
To determine compliance with internally-defined vendor processes
To determine compliance with signed vendor agreements/contracts
To ensure your entitlements do not exceed your allocations
To determine compliance with licensing agreements regarding who, how, and when freeware software is being used

questions.explanation: The purpose of an external audit is to determine compliance with signed vendor agreements/contracts. Software publishers conduct audits to verify that organizations are using their software in accordance with the license terms they purchased. Non-compliance can result in significant financial penalties and remediation costs.

questions.stem:
HOTSPOT -
Match terms with the definitions related to Strategic Conformance:
questions.explanation: This is a HOTSPOT matching question about Strategic Conformance terms and definitions. Strategic Conformance in SAM evaluates whether software usage aligns with organizational licensing strategy. Key terms include: Compliant (usage within entitlements), Non-Compliant (usage exceeds entitlements), Over-Licensed (more licenses than needed), and Under-Licensed (insufficient licenses for usage). Without the exhibit, exact matching cannot be confirmed.

questions.stem: Software Asset Lifecycle has __________ components.
questions.explanation: The Software Asset Lifecycle has 8 components. These typically include: Plan, Source, Receive, Deploy, Manage, Support, Optimize, and Sunset/Retire. Each component represents a stage in managing software from initial planning through retirement.

questions.stem: Additional Software Model Lifecycles phases can be added as __________ .
questions.explanation: Additional Software Model Lifecycle phases can be added as Choices. In ServiceNow, the lifecycle phase field uses the Choice data type (sys_choice table), so new phases are added by creating new choice values. This is consistent with how ServiceNow extends selection fields.

questions.stem: Software Model Lifecycles can only be created for an external, publisher defined date.
questions.explanation: This is false. Software Model Lifecycles can be created for both external publisher-defined dates AND internally-defined dates. Organizations can set their own lifecycle milestones (like internal EOL recommendations or migration deadlines) independent of the publisher's official dates. The Content Service provides publisher dates, but custom entries can supplement them.

questions.stem: Once a weekly software content update adds lifecycle data to your instance, can it be deleted from the software model?

options.text: It can be deleted or deactivated
It cannot unless the lifecycle stage is EOL

questions.explanation: No, once a weekly software content update adds lifecycle data to your instance, it cannot be deleted from the software model. The Content Service lifecycle data is managed centrally and protected from local deletion to maintain data integrity. This ensures consistent lifecycle tracking across the platform.

questions.stem: During contract negotiations, what report could you run to gain visibility to products nearing end-of support?
questions.explanation: The Software Model Lifecycle Report provides visibility to products nearing end-of-support, which is valuable during contract negotiations. This report shows lifecycle stages including general availability, end-of-sale, end-of-support, and end-of-life dates for software models, helping inform renewal and migration decisions.

questions.stem: Once you are ready to retire software in ServiceNow, what is the critical first step in the retirement process?

options.text: Manually set Allocations available on the entitlement to Zero (0)
Run the Software Model Lifecycle Report

questions.explanation: The critical first step in the software retirement process is to expire identified active software entitlements. This prevents new allocations from being created and signals that the software is being retired. After expiring entitlements, you then revoke allocations, reclaim installations, and complete the retirement. Expiring entitlements first ensures no new rights are distributed.

questions.stem: Publisher information such as general availability and end-of-life dates will be provided as part of what feature within ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: Software model lifecycle provides publisher information such as general availability (GA) and end-of-life (EOL) dates within ServiceNow. The Content Service downloads these dates and associates them with software models. Publisher packs (C) provide license metrics, not lifecycle dates. Normalization suggestions (D) help with discovery model cleanup.

questions.stem:
A user is notified their software install has been flagged for reclamation. The user declines approval.
What is the next step in the workflow?

options.text: The user’s manager must approve or decline the reclamation.
The reclamation candidate is removed from the candidate list.
The software is reclaimed since it was not in use.

questions.explanation: When a user declines the reclamation approval, the next step in the workflow is that the user's manager must approve or decline the reclamation. This two-tier approval process ensures that low-usage software isn't automatically reclaimed if the user objects — their manager makes the final decision on whether the software is still needed.

questions.stem: Which of the following features enables organizations to easily upgrade a standard version of their software to an enterprise version?
questions.explanation: Software Assurance enables organizations to easily upgrade a standard version of software to an enterprise version. Software Assurance (SA) is a Microsoft maintenance program that grants upgrade rights. In ServiceNow SAM, SA entitlements allow step-up from standard to enterprise editions. Allocations (D) assign rights but don't enable upgrades.

questions.stem: What role must be granted in order to create new reports that could be viewed by other people?
questions.explanation: The Global Report User (report_global) role must be granted to create new reports viewable by other people. This role allows a user to create reports that are visible to others in the organization. Report_Creator (A) is not a standard role name, report_publisher (B) is for publishing, and itil (C) doesn't grant global report creation privileges.

questions.stem: Performance Analytics allows users to: (Choose three.)

options.text: Track usage of a particular software.
Assess publisher compliance over a period of time.
View trends of software license allocations.

questions.explanation: Performance Analytics in SAM allows users to: (A) track usage of a particular software, (B) assess publisher compliance over a period of time, and (D) view trends of software license allocations. PA provides trend analysis and dashboards for software asset data. Configuring software reclamation (C) is an administrative SAM function, not a PA capability — reclamation uses rules and workflows, not analytics.

questions.stem: Software Asset Management (SAM) Professional reports can be delivered in which formats? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Software Asset Management Professional reports can be delivered in PDF (B), CSV (C), and XLS (D) formats. These are the standard export formats for ServiceNow reports. PowerPoint (A) is not a supported report delivery format in the baseline ServiceNow reporting engine.

questions.stem: The goals of Software Asset Management include which of the following? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The goals of Software Asset Management include: Optimize spend (A) — reduce costs through reclamation and right-sizing, Maintain compliance (C) — ensure license agreements are honored, and Support software audits (E) — provide accurate data for vendor audits. Rationalizing business applications (B) is more of an APM goal, and identifying unauthorized usage (D), while a benefit, is not a primary stated goal.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow plugin is used by Software Asset Management (SAM) Professional and configured during SAM Professional setup?
questions.explanation: Normalization Data Services is the plugin used by SAM Professional and configured during SAM Professional setup. This plugin provides the Content Service integration that downloads normalization content, publisher part numbers, lifecycle data, and discovery model mappings from ServiceNow's central library. It is essential for the normalization process.

questions.stem: Which SAM role must be a trained ServiceNow administrator?
questions.explanation: The sam_developer role must be a trained ServiceNow administrator. The sam_developer handles custom license scripts, business rules, and technical configurations within SAM that require deep ServiceNow platform knowledge. The sam_admin (A) manages SAM operations but doesn't need full platform admin training — the sam_developer needs both SAM and platform expertise.

questions.stem: Within Software Asset Management there are many key terms to understand, what is the best definition for Reconciliation?

options.text: Software license details that define use rights
One or more use rights assigned to a specific device or user
The process of standardizing discovered software installation data to defined norms
The process of producing a compliance position by comparing the number of software rights acquired against the normalized software inventory

questions.explanation: Reconciliation is the process of producing a compliance position by comparing the number of software rights acquired against the normalized software inventory. It determines whether an organization is compliant, over-licensed, or under-licensed for each product. Options A/B describe entitlements/allocations, C describes modeling, and D describes normalization.

questions.stem: By default, which persona is responsible for loading asset management data from integrations and discovery tools into SAM Pro?
questions.explanation: The ServiceNow administrator is responsible for loading asset management data from integrations and discovery tools into SAM Professional. This is a platform-level technical task involving data imports, integration configuration, and discovery setup that falls under the ServiceNow admin's responsibilities, not the SAM manager or SAM user.

questions.stem: As part of the discovery process, when records are written to the software installation table a check is performed to determine if the information already exists in the discovery model table, if a record exists, what does the system do?

options.text: The record is deleted and recreated to ensure the most recent discovery model is recorded.
Nothing, the record exists so it is ignored.
A new record is created for the installation in the discovery model table.
A reference to the discovery model record is identified and associated to the software installation record.

questions.explanation: When records are written to the software installation table and the discovery model already exists, the system identifies a reference to the existing discovery model record and associates it to the software installation record. This prevents duplicate discovery models — each unique software identity has one discovery model that multiple installations reference.

questions.stem: Which of the following are valid on import errors (vs. after import) when using the automated entitlement import feature? (Choose three.)

options.text: Purchased rights should be greater than 0
The end date must be greater than the start date
Publisher Part Number and Software Model not found

questions.explanation: Valid on-import errors (during import, not after) include: Purchased rights should be greater than 0 (A) — validates the rights value, Publisher Part Number and Software Model not found (C) — no matching PPN or model exists, and Duplicate entry (D) — the entitlement already exists. End date > start date (B) is an after-import validation. 'PPN already exists' (E) is not an error during import.

questions.stem: What are the available actions associated with the Normalization Suggestions feature? (Choose two.)

options.text: Accept – updates the discovery model with suggested values
Reject – ignores the suggestion. The next time the scheduled job is executed, it will not pick the same package or rule that was rejected previously
Save – allows you to save the suggestion to review again later
Ignore – ignores the suggestion. All fields are updated to read only until the next time the job is executed with the same package or rule that was ignored previously.
Create – creates a discovery model with suggested values

questions.explanation: The available actions for Normalization Suggestions are: Accept (A) — updates the discovery model with the suggested normalized values, and Reject (B) — ignores the suggestion, and the next scheduled job run will not pick the same package or rule that was rejected. Save (C), Ignore (D), and Create (E) are not valid actions in the Normalization Suggestions feature.

questions.stem: What is used to identify and normalize software installed in an environment?
questions.explanation: Software Discovery Models are used to identify and normalize software installed in the environment. Each discovery model represents a unique combination of publisher, product, and version as found by Discovery. The normalization process then maps these discovery models to standardized software models in the content library.

questions.stem: When a software title is transferred between vendors, the content library download and update feature will automatically propagate those changes to which of the following? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: When a software title is transferred between vendors, the content library update automatically propagates changes to Software Entitlements (A), Software Models (C), and Discovery Models (E). This ensures all related records reflect the new publisher/vendor information without manual updates. Reconciliations (B) are recalculated, not directly updated, and Transform Maps (D) are not affected.

questions.stem: When creating a transform map to map software installation data into the appropriate SAM table, why would you set the coalesce values for the u_display_name. u_publisher, u_version, u_installed_on, and u_assigned_to fields to be true? (Choose two.)

options.text: To ensure that you import all these fields into the table
To ensure that if all fields match an existing record on import, that a new record is created
To ensure that if all fields do not match an existing record on import, that a new record is created

questions.explanation: Setting coalesce on display_name, publisher, version, installed_on, and assigned_to fields serves to: avoid duplication of data (B) — by identifying existing records that match all coalesced fields, and ensure that if all fields do NOT match an existing record, a new record is created (E). Coalesce determines the unique key for matching — if all match, update; if any don't match, create new.

questions.stem: What information is required when importing device allocations? (Choose three.)

options.text: Software model associated with the allocation
Quantity of rights allocated to the device

questions.explanation: When importing device allocations, you need: Software model associated with the allocation (A), Entitlement associated with the allocation (D), and Quantity of rights allocated to the device (E). The software model identifies what software, the entitlement identifies the license source, and the quantity specifies how many rights. Purchase order (B) and user assigned (C) are not required for device allocations.

questions.stem: Within ServiceNow Discovery, the Scanning phase determines what?

options.text: What else can you tell me about yourself?
How should I classify you specifically?
Are you there? How will I classify you?

questions.explanation: The Scanning phase of Discovery determines 'Are you there? How will I classify you?' Scanning is the first phase that probes IP ranges to find active devices and determine basic device type for classification. Exploration (A) gathers details, Classification (B) assigns specific type, and Identification (C) checks for existing records.

questions.stem: Software models are used to connect purchased software rights with discovered software installations via which mechanism?
questions.explanation: Software models connect purchased software rights with discovered installations via the Software Discovery Map. The discovery map links discovery model data (from installations) to software models (associated with entitlements), bridging the gap between what's discovered and what's licensed. This mapping enables reconciliation to compare rights against usage.

questions.stem: What are three ways to get software asset data into ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: The three standard ways to get software asset data into ServiceNow are Discovery, Import Data, and Manual entry. Discovery automatically finds software on the network through scanning. Import Data uses import sets to bulk-load data from external sources (CSV, LDAP, etc.). Manual entry involves creating records directly through ServiceNow forms. These cover all data volume levels from small to large.

questions.stem: ServiceNow Discovery finds IP-enabled devices and the software that runs on them. It uses a combination of the following methods to explore the devices. (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: ServiceNow Discovery uses Patterns (C), Probes (D), and Sensors (E) to explore devices. Patterns are the modern approach using JavaScript to define discovery logic. Probes are sent to the MID Server to gather data from devices, and Sensors process the data returned by probes. Discovery is agentless — it does not use agents (A) installed on target devices.

questions.stem: What does the acronym “CAL” stand for?
questions.explanation: CAL stands for Client Access License. It grants the right for a user or device to access server-based software (like Microsoft SQL Server or Windows Server). CALs are one of the most common licensing models in enterprise software and are tracked as license metrics in SAM.

questions.stem: Within the ‘Run Reconciliation’ process, how can the reconciliation be grouped?

options.text: Country, Department, Company, Region, Cost Center
Country, Business Unit, Corporation, Location, Account
Country, Business Unit, Company, Region, Cost Center

questions.explanation: Reconciliation can be grouped by Country, Department, Company, Region, and Cost Center. These grouping dimensions allow organizations to view compliance positions segmented by organizational or geographic criteria, which is useful for managing software across business units or locations.

questions.stem: By default, which ServiceNow role can read, but not create, a custom license script?
questions.explanation: The sam_admin role can read but NOT create custom license scripts by default. Only the sam_developer role has permission to create and modify custom license scripts. The sam_admin has read access to understand the scripts being used, but script creation is restricted to the developer role for safety and governance.

questions.stem: Which of the following is set in a software entitlement and used during reconciliation to determine your compliance position?
questions.explanation: The License Metric set in a software entitlement is used during reconciliation to determine the compliance position. It defines how software rights are counted (per user, per device, per core, etc.) and determines the calculation method for comparing purchased rights against discovered installations.

questions.stem: Once downgrade rights have been populated in the Downgrade Rights table, can they be deleted?

options.text: They can be deleted or deactivated
They cannot until all associated allocations have been removed

questions.explanation: No, once downgrade rights have been populated in the Downgrade Rights table, they cannot be deleted. Like Content Service lifecycle data, downgrade rights are protected from deletion to maintain the integrity of the licensing hierarchy. This prevents accidental removal of important version relationship data.

questions.stem: By default, which ServiceNow role can run on-demand reconciliation?
questions.explanation: The sam_admin role can run on-demand reconciliation by default. Running reconciliation is an administrative SAM operation that triggers the compliance calculation engine. The sam_user role (A) can only view results. There is no sam_reconcile_user (B) or sam_manager (E) role in baseline SAM.

questions.stem: On the License Workbench, which of the following is defined as the “Estimated cost of remediating non-compliance”?
questions.explanation: True-up cost is defined as the estimated cost of remediating non-compliance on the License Workbench.
