It calculates the cost of purchasing additional licenses needed to become compliant. Software spend (A) is total cost, Reconciliation cost (B) is not a standard term, True-down cost (C) represents savings from over-licensing, and Over-licensed cost (D) is the excess spend.

questions.stem: Automated license reconciliation keeps license positions accurate and up-to-date without manual calculations. Disregarding on-demand runs for a specific publisher or all publishers, how often does reconciliation run?
questions.explanation: Automated license reconciliation runs weekly by default, disregarding on-demand runs. The weekly scheduled job processes all publishers and generates updated compliance results. This provides a regular cadence for maintaining up-to-date license positions without manual intervention.

questions.stem: When reconciliation is run, what information does the software product results display?

options.text: Results for all products and installations associated to the publisher
Results for each license metric associated to the software model
Results for all models and installations associated to the product
Results for all license metrics related to the software model

questions.explanation: Software product results display results for all models and installations associated to the product. This is the product-level tier of reconciliation, aggregating compliance data from all software models (versions/editions) and their installations under a single product. Publisher results (A) are one level higher, and license metric results (B/D) are one level lower.

questions.stem: When reconciliation is run, what information does the software publisher results display?

options.text: Results for all products and installations associated to the publisher
Results for each license metric associated to the software model
Results for all models and installations associated to the product
Results for all license metrics related to the software model

questions.explanation: Software publisher results display results for all products and installations associated to the publisher. This is the highest tier of reconciliation results, showing the aggregate compliance position across all of a publisher's software products. It provides the broadest view for vendor-level compliance analysis.

questions.stem: What type of record is only created when a software model or entitlement exists for the product?
questions.explanation: Software Model Results are only created when a software model or entitlement exists for the product. This is because model-level results require a defined software model to calculate compliance against. Product results are generated for all licensable products, but model results specifically require a software model or entitlement to be present.

questions.stem: For which of the following reasons could an installation be unlicensed at the Product Result level?

options.text: The software installation was not completed correctly due to an incorrect workflow set-up.
Software installation records are not associated with a software discovery model.
The software normalization process has not yet run.
The software discovery model is not mapped to the appropriate software model.
The software installation has not been fully reconciled.

questions.explanation: An installation could be unlicensed at the Product Result level because software installation records are not associated with a software discovery model. Without a discovery model link, the installation cannot be normalized and mapped to a software model, leaving it unrecognized in reconciliation and appearing as unlicensed at the product level.

questions.stem: By default, which ServiceNow role can only view reconciliation results?
questions.explanation: The sam_user role can only view reconciliation results by default. It provides read-only access to reconciliation data including product results, model results, and license metrics. The sam_admin (D) can both view and act on results. There is no sam_viewer (C), sam_reconcile_user (A), or sam_cmdb_user (D) in baseline SAM.

questions.stem: For products monitored by System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM), what usage data point(s) are imported for reclamation analysis?

options.text: Last Used and Total Usage Time

questions.explanation: For products monitored by SCCM, the usage data points imported for reclamation analysis are Last Used and Total Usage Time. These two data points allow reclamation rules to evaluate both when software was last used and how long it has been used in total, identifying candidates where the software is underutilized or abandoned.

questions.stem: Which catalog provides a collection of models in the environment?
questions.explanation: The Product Catalog provides a collection of models in the environment. It serves as the internal inventory of known and approved software and hardware models that the organization manages. The Service Catalog (A) is for requests, the Vendor Catalog (D) is for vendor offerings, and Model Catalog (E) is a broader term not used as a specific SAM catalog.

questions.stem: Software reclamation is integrated with which of the following to automate the process of uninstalling software from devices and reclaiming those software rights?
questions.explanation: Software reclamation is integrated with Client Software Distribution (CSD) to automate the process of uninstalling software from devices and reclaiming those software rights. CSD (powered by Orchestration) remotely removes the software from the device, allowing the freed license to be reallocated.

questions.stem: Reclamation rules can be applied to what types of software? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Reclamation rules can be applied to Subscription software (A) and Installed software (D). Subscription software may be reclaimed when subscriptions expire or usage drops, and installed software is reclaimed based on usage metrics. End-of-life software (B) is handled through retirement, blacklisted software (C) through removal policies, and freeware (E) typically doesn't need reclamation.

questions.stem: Which of the following are valid Remediation Options on the License Workbench after reconciliation has been run? (Choose five.)
questions.explanation: The valid remediation options after reconciliation are: Purchase Rights (C), Remove Unallocated Installs (D), Remove Unlicensed Installs (E), Create Allocations (F), and Remove Allocation (G). Create Entitlements (A) is done through the purchase process, not as a direct remediation option. Remove Metric Attributes (B) is not a remediation option.

questions.stem: Which of the following are valid States of Remediation Options on the License Workbench after a reconciliation has been run? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The valid states of remediation options are: New (A) — just created, Cancelled (B) — cancelled by user, Complete (D) — finished successfully, and In Progress (F) — workflow/process underway. Void (C) and Done (E) are not valid remediation option states in the baseline configuration.

questions.stem: What role(s) are required to import financial data for use in software spend detection? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: To import financial data for software spend detection, the sam_user (implied via sam_admin) and sam_admin (D) roles are required. The sam_admin role provides full access to SAM administration including data import functions. The sam_user (C) provides basic access. Together with sam_admin, these cover the required permissions for spend data import.

questions.stem: What type of publisher lifecycle information does the Software Lifecycle report prioritize?

options.text: Information provided in the demo data
Information provided by the software library
Information provided by the publisher pack

questions.explanation: The Software Lifecycle report prioritizes information entered by the user. User-entered lifecycle data takes precedence over publisher-provided data from the content library, demo data, or publisher pack data. This allows organizations to override publisher dates with their own planned dates for internal lifecycle management.

questions.stem: Maintenance entitlements can be associated with what types of entitlements (for non-Microsoft publishers)? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: For non-Microsoft publishers, maintenance entitlements can be associated with Upgrade (A), Perpetual (B), and Perpetual + Maintenance (D) entitlement types. Subscription (E) and Perpetual + Subscription (C) are not valid types for maintenance entitlement association in the baseline configuration for non-Microsoft publishers.

questions.stem: How are Microsoft Office 365 reserved licenses handled after true-up?

options.text: They are automatically converted into regular licenses
They are automatically disabled until additional licenses are purchased
They are automatically deleted and must be re-reserved
They are automatically removed from true-up calculations and billed separately

questions.explanation: After true-up, Microsoft Office 365 reserved licenses are automatically converted into regular licenses. The true-up process reconciles reserved (placeholder) licenses with actual usage, converting them to standard active licenses. This ensures accurate license counts and billing alignment with Microsoft's subscription model.

questions.stem: Using end-of-life/end-of-support software exposes your organization to security threats. What report can you run to gain visibility to these products?

options.text: Software Models with deactivated discovery maps

questions.explanation: The Software Product Lifecycle Report provides visibility to products using end-of-life or end-of-support software. This report shows lifecycle stages at the product level, highlighting security exposure from running unsupported software. The Software Model Lifecycle Report (C) shows model-level detail, but the Product level report is specifically designed for this security visibility.

questions.stem: Performance Analytics allows users to do which of the following? (Choose three.)

options.text: Assess publisher compliance over a period of time
View trends of software license allocations
Track usage of a particular software

questions.explanation: Performance Analytics allows users to: Assess publisher compliance over a period of time (A) via trend analysis, View trends of software license allocations (B) to track allocation changes, and Track usage of a particular software (E) through usage indicators. Configure software reclamation (C) and Remediate non-compliance (D) are operational actions done in SAM, not PA capabilities.

questions.stem:
A user is notified their software install has been flagged for reclamation. The user declines approval.
What is the next step in the workflow?

options.text: The user’s manager must approve or decline the reclamation.
The reclamation candidate is removed from the candidate list.
The software is reclaimed since it was not in use the notification was only informational.
A justification is requested and submitted to Change Management for approval.

questions.explanation: When a user declines the reclamation approval, the next step in the workflow is that the user's manager must approve or decline the reclamation. The two-tier approval workflow escalates to the manager when the end user objects. The manager makes the final decision on whether the software is business-critical or can be reclaimed.

questions.stem: What does a usage record track?

options.text: The sum of usage for a selected data
The high watermark of software usage
The sum of usage on a weekly basis
The sum of usage since installation date
The sum of usage on a monthly basis

questions.explanation: A usage record tracks the sum of usage on a monthly basis. Software usage records aggregate usage data (time used, last used) into monthly periods, providing a consistent time-based view for reclamation analysis and compliance reporting. This monthly granularity balances detail with manageable data volumes.

questions.stem: Within ServiceNow Discovery, the Classification phase determines what?

options.text: Are you there? How will I classify you?
How should I classify you specifically?
What else can you tell me about yourself?

questions.explanation: The Classification phase of Discovery determines 'How should I classify you specifically?' During Classification, Discovery determines the specific device type (Windows server, Linux workstation, network switch, etc.) based on the initial scan results. Scanning (A) asks 'Are you there?', Identification (B) asks 'Have I seen you before?', and Exploration (D) asks 'What else?'.

questions.stem: When loading a large amount of software installation data, which is the best method to use?
questions.explanation: For loading a large amount of software installation data, Discovery is the best method. Discovery automatically scans the environment and populates the software installation table at scale. Import data (D) is better for medium amounts, and manual entry (C) is for small amounts. Workflow (B) and business rules (E) are not data loading methods.

questions.stem: The Per Named User license metric licenses which of the following?

options.text: A user for a number of installations of software
A device for a number of installations of software
A specific user for a number of installations of software
Cores on a physical server or virtual machine
A specific device for a number of installations of software

questions.explanation: Per Named User licenses a specific user for a number of installations of software. The key word is 'specific' — a Named User license is tied to an identified individual, regardless of how many devices they use the software on. Option A describes a general per-user metric without the 'named' specificity.

questions.stem: What type of record is only created when a software model or entitlement exists for the product?
questions.explanation: Software Model Results are only created when a software model or entitlement exists for the product. Without a defined software model or associated entitlement, there is nothing to reconcile at the model level. Product results may exist showing unlicensed installations, but model results require a model definition.

questions.stem: Which of the following are tiers of software reconciliation results? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Software License Metric (D) and Software Product (E) are tiers of software reconciliation results. The four tiers are: Publisher → Product → Model → License Metric. Software Allocation (A), Software Vendor (B — not a tier name), and Software Entitlement (C) are inputs to reconciliation, not result tiers.

questions.stem: Baseline license metrics are defined for which of the following? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Baseline license metrics are defined for Cores (A), Devices (D), and Processors (F). These are the out-of-box hardware-oriented metrics. User-based metrics like Per Named User also exist but are defined for users, not listed here. Metric Types (B), Publishers (C), and Operating Systems (E) are not what metrics are defined FOR — they are classification or grouping concepts.

questions.stem: Which of the following are valid Remediation Options on the License Workbench after reconciliation has been run? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Valid remediation options on the License Workbench include: Remove Allocations (B), Remove Unallocated Installs (C), and Remove Unlicensed Installs (D). Create Entitlements (A) is typically done via purchase orders, not as a direct remediation option. Remove Metric Attributes (E) is not a remediation action.

questions.stem: Which of the following are valid States of Remediation Options on the License Workbench after reconciliation has been run? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Valid states of remediation options are: Complete (A) — finished, New (B) — just created, and In Progress (E) — workflow underway. Done (C) is not a valid state (Complete is used instead). Cancelled (D) is also a valid state but only three were requested, and the most commonly referenced states are New, In Progress, and Complete.

questions.stem: What are Restricted software installations?

options.text: Software installations that are unlicensed and unallocated
Software installations that are not normalized
Software installations that are unauthorized for use

questions.explanation: Restricted software installations are software installations that are unauthorized for use in the environment. Unlike blacklisted software (which is completely banned), restricted software may have limited authorized use but is flagged when found outside approved scope. This helps enforce organizational software policies.

questions.stem: Once you are ready to retire software in ServiceNow, what is the critical first step in the retirement process?

options.text: Notify users of the software retirement
Uninstall all instances of the software

questions.explanation: The critical first step in software retirement is to expire any active software entitlements. This prevents new allocations and signals that the software rights are no longer valid. After expiring entitlements, you proceed to revoke allocations, notify users, uninstall the software, and complete the retirement process.

questions.stem: After importing your entitlements via the template where would you navigate to address any entitlement import errors?

options.text: System Import Sets > Load Data > Entitlement Import Errors
Software Asset > Licensing > Entitlement import Errors

questions.explanation: After importing entitlements via the template, navigate to Software Asset > Licensing > Entitlement Import Errors to address any errors. This module shows records that failed import validation (missing PPN, duplicate entries, invalid data) and provides actions to resolve them (create, reject, delete).

questions.stem: Which are valid States of Remediation Options on the Software Asset Workspace License usage view after reconciliation has been run? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Valid states of remediation options on the Software Asset Workspace License usage view are: In Progress (A), Complete (D), and New (E). These mirror the standard remediation states. Done (B) and Cancelled (C) are not the primary states shown on the workspace view. The workspace displays the current status of ongoing remediation activities.

questions.stem: Which tab of the License usage view is used to reclaim software licenses that are not being used?
questions.explanation: The Removal Candidates tab on the License usage view is used to reclaim software licenses that are not being used. This tab lists software installations flagged for removal through reclamation rules, manual addition, or remediation actions, enabling the SAM team to initiate the uninstall and right recovery process.

questions.stem: Which feature provides detailed, actionable information for software reconciliation?

options.text: Software Asset Workspace Success portal view
Software Asset Workspace Software asset analytics view
Software Asset Workspace License usage view
Software Asset Workspace License operations view
Software Asset Workspace Normalization suggestions view

questions.explanation: The Software Asset Workspace License usage view provides detailed, actionable information for software reconciliation. This is the modern workspace equivalent of the classic License Workbench, offering reconciliation results, remediation options, removal candidates, and compliance status in the new UI paradigm.

questions.stem: By default, which persona is responsible for ensuring that the SAM program is rolled out and executed correctly and consistently across the organization?
questions.explanation: The SAM process owner is responsible for ensuring the SAM program is rolled out and executed correctly and consistently across the organization. The process owner sets strategy, governance, and standards. The SAM manager (D) handles day-to-day operations, and the SAM administrator (E) handles technical configuration.

questions.stem: Which role is required to create custom license metrics?
questions.explanation: The sam_developer role is required to create custom license metrics. Custom metrics involve writing scripts that define how software rights are calculated for non-standard licensing models. This requires the scripting capability granted by the sam_developer role. The sam_admin (A) can view but not create custom metrics.

questions.stem: What Microsoft maintenance program enables you to step up a standard version of your software to an enterprise edition?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Software Assurance (SA) is the maintenance program that enables stepping up from a standard version of software to an enterprise edition. Software Assurance provides upgrade rights, including version upgrades and edition step-ups, along with other benefits like training vouchers and deployment planning services.

questions.stem: During the Source Request task, the SAM manage or administrator has what options? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: During the Source Request task, the SAM manager or administrator has two options: Add purchase order (A) to procure new licenses for the requested software, or Add allocation (E) to assign existing available entitlement rights to the requester. These represent the two ways to fulfill a software request — buy new or allocate existing.

questions.stem: When importing and/or manually entering software entitlement data into SAM you find that you do not have the Publisher Part Number (PPN) for several of your entitlements. What essential information is required in order for you to successfully add these entitlement records?

options.text: Agreement type, Purchased rights, Product, Asset tag, and Vendor
Publisher, Product, Version, Edition, Platform, and Language
Publisher, Product, License type, Purchased rights, Metric group, and License metric
Version, Edition, Platform, Purchased rights, Vendor, and Contract number

questions.explanation: When Publisher Part Number (PPN) is not available, you need: Publisher, Product, License type, Purchased rights, Metric group, and License metric to successfully add entitlement records. These fields collectively identify the software, define the licensing model, and specify the number of rights — enough for SAM to create and reconcile the entitlement without a PPN lookup.

questions.stem: Which application or feature can be used in baseline Software Asset Management (SAM) Professional to import software usage data?
questions.explanation: SCCM (System Center Configuration Manager) is the application available in baseline SAM Professional to import software usage data. ServiceNow provides dedicated SCCM integration plugins for usage data import. Other third-party sources (A) are not baseline, APM (B) is Application Portfolio Management, and Discovery (C) finds installations but doesn't collect usage metrics.

questions.stem: What methods can you use to store contract terms with your contracts? (Choose two.)

options.text: Attach a PDF of the contract to the contract record
Add the details in the Terms and Conditions section of the contract record
Add a link m the software entitlement record to the contract details stored in another location
Add the details in the Contract section of the software entitlement record
Add a link to the contract details the Assets covered record

questions.explanation: You can store contract terms by attaching a PDF of the contract to the contract record (A) and by adding details in the Terms and Conditions section of the contract record (B). These two methods provide both document storage and structured data entry. Adding links to external locations (C) or using entitlement records (D) are not standard methods for storing contract terms.

questions.stem: When using the ServiceNow Client Software Distribution (CSD) product in conjunction with Microsoft System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM) to automatically remove software and reclaim license rights in your environment which of the following is required?

options.text: The software to be removed must have been installed by SCCM
You must purchase Orchestration separately in order to revoke software and reclaim license rights using SAM Pro
The software to be removed must have been discovered by SCCM
An SCCM configuration record must be created to identify the application and the associated software discovery mode

questions.explanation: When using CSD with SCCM to automatically remove software and reclaim licenses, an SCCM configuration record must be created to identify the application and the associated software discovery model. This configuration links the SCCM application to the SAM discovery model so CSD knows which software to target for removal.

questions.stem: What SAM feature automatically adds the next version and downgrade rights to a software model?
questions.explanation: The Content Service automatically adds the next version and downgrade rights to a software model. When the Content Service downloads updated content from ServiceNow's central library, it includes version relationships and downgrade right mappings that are applied to software models automatically. Discovery models (D) don't add rights, and entitlements (C) are created from purchases.

questions.stem: License Change Projection works for which of the following change types? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: License Change Projection works for Normal (A) and Emergency (E) change types. These change types may affect software installations (adding or removing software), and License Change Projection evaluates the impact on license compliance before the change is implemented. Standard (B) changes use pre-approved templates that don't typically need license projection.

questions.stem: What is the definition of Partially Normalized?

options.text: A discovery model was normalized based on publisher product version fields
A discovery model was normalized based on publisher field a one
A discovery model was normalized based on publisher and product fields only
The software discovery model has not yet competed its run through the normalization process
A discovery model normalized based on product field alone

questions.explanation: Partially Normalized means a discovery model was normalized based on publisher and product fields only, without version information. Full normalization includes publisher, product, version, and edition. When only publisher and product can be matched, the status is Partially Normalized, indicating incomplete normalization data.

questions.stem: Which of the following license metrics require allocations in order to maintain compliance? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Per Named User (C) and Per Named Device (D) license metrics require allocations to maintain compliance. 'Named' metrics tie rights to specific identified users or devices, requiring explicit allocation records. Per Core (A), Per Device (B without 'Named'), and Per User (E without 'Named') calculate compliance without individual allocations.

questions.stem: When Discovery identifies installed software in your environment, what table does it automatically store this data in?
questions.explanation: When Discovery identifies installed software, it automatically stores the data in the Software Installation table [cmdb_sam_sw_install]. This is the core SAM table for tracking all software installations across managed devices. The legacy table was cmdb_ci_spkg, but SAM Professional uses cmdb_sam_sw_install.

questions.stem: What navigational functions does the Software Asset Workspace License usage view provide on the product Details tab? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The Software Asset Workspace License usage view Product Details tab provides: Filter products (C) to search for specific products, Expand and collapse tree links (D) for navigation, and Expand All (E) to show the full hierarchy. Remediation options (A) and Unlicensed installs (B) are available on other tabs/sections, not as navigation functions on the Product Details tab.

questions.stem: Where can the Software Model Results, Removal Candidates, Entitlements, and Remediation Options related lists be accessed on the Software Asset Workspace after a reconciliation is run?
questions.explanation: The Software Model Results, Removal Candidates, Entitlements, and Remediation Options related lists are all accessible from the License usage view in the Software Asset Workspace after reconciliation runs. This consolidated view provides all the key reconciliation outputs and actions in one place.

questions.stem: Software discovery models are stored in which table?
questions.explanation: Software discovery models are stored in the cmdb_sam_sw_discovery_model table (option D despite the typo in the answer text). This table stores the raw discovery model data including publisher, product, and version as discovered, before normalization. The other options reference non-existent or incorrect table names.

questions.stem: What are Microsoft Office 365 reserved licenses used tor?

options.text: To reserve a block of licenses for a specific group of users and/or user role(s)
To convert subscription licenses to regular per device licenses
To accurately calculate annual true-up cost and total spend on a product
To convert regular per user licenses into subscription licenses

questions.explanation: Microsoft Office 365 reserved licenses are used to accurately calculate annual true-up cost and total spend on a product. Reserved licenses represent allocated but not yet assigned licenses that factor into true-up cost calculations during reconciliation. They help organizations plan for upcoming license needs and budget accordingly.

questions.stem: Which SAM role grants a user the ability to set reclamation rules?
questions.explanation: The sam_admin role grants the ability to set reclamation rules. Reclamation rule configuration is an administrative SAM function that requires sam_admin privileges. The sam_user (C) can only view, and sam_integrator (B) and sam_analyst (D) are not standard baseline SAM roles.

questions.stem: To accurately report your true up costs during reconciliation, what must you update In your software models? (Choose two.)

options.text: License cost plus reserve license cost
License cost plus maintenance cost plus reserved license cost

questions.explanation: To accurately report true-up costs during reconciliation, you must update License cost (A) and Maintenance cost (D) in your software models. License cost defines the per-unit cost for calculating true-up (cost to purchase additional licenses for compliance), and Maintenance cost is included because ongoing maintenance is typically required with new license purchases. Both feed into the true-up cost calculation.

questions.stem: When creating entitlements on the Software Entitlement Form and selecting a product Publisher Part Number (PPN), what information is defaulted from the PPN? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: When selecting a Publisher Part Number (PPN) on the Software Entitlement form, the License metric (A) and License type (C) are automatically defaulted from the PPN record. PPNs in the Content Service library contain pre-configured licensing attributes that auto-populate the entitlement fields, ensuring accurate metric and type assignment.

questions.stem: When creating a purchase order, which feature allows sourcing a software model from multiple providers?
questions.explanation: The Vendor Catalog item allows sourcing a software model from multiple providers when creating a purchase order. Vendor Catalog items represent different vendor offerings for the same product, enabling comparison shopping across vendors. A regular Catalog item (A) represents a single sourcing path.

questions.stem: Using content library data to track a software model’s lifecycle phase assists which ServiceNow product to perform application rationalization?
questions.explanation: Software model lifecycle phase data from the content library assists Technology Portfolio Management (TPM) to perform application rationalization. TPM uses lifecycle data (EOL, EOS dates) to identify aging technology that should be migrated or retired, supporting portfolio optimization decisions.

questions.stem: Which consolidated dashboard in the new SAM Professional workspace enables you to organize, evaluate and view key metrics for Microsoft Office 365 and Adobe Cloud?
questions.explanation: The SaaS overview dashboard in the new SAM Professional workspace is the consolidated dashboard for organizing, evaluating, and viewing key metrics for Microsoft Office 365 and Adobe Cloud subscriptions. This dashboard is designed specifically for SaaS subscription management and optimization.

questions.stem: During the normalization process a discovery model can be fully normalized based on which of these fields? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: A discovery model can be fully normalized based on Product (A), Version (C), and Publisher (F). Full normalization requires matching all three fields — publisher, product, and version — to content library entries. Asset tag (B), license metric (D), and vendor (E) are not normalization fields. Partial normalization occurs when only publisher and product match.

questions.stem: Within ServiceNow Discovery, the Identification phase determines what?

options.text: How should I classify you specifically?
What else can you tell me about yourself?
Are you there? How will I classify you?

questions.explanation: The Identification phase of Discovery determines 'Have I seen you before?' During Identification, Discovery checks whether the discovered device matches an existing CI in the CMDB. If a match is found, the existing CI is updated; if not, a new CI is created. Scanning asks 'Are you there?', Classification asks 'How to classify?', and Exploration gathers details.

questions.stem: What is unmanaged spend when viewing the Software Spend Detection Overview dashboard?

options.text: The total spend for transactions where the publisher and product are identified but there's no software model identified for the product
The total spend for transactions where the publisher, product, and software model are identified but there's no software installations identified for the product
The total spend for transactions that are not identified as an accounts payable spend or an expense spend
The total spend for transactions that are identified for an unmanaged publisher

questions.explanation: Unmanaged spend is the total spend for transactions where the publisher and product are identified but there is no software model identified for the product. This means the organization is spending money on software that isn't properly modeled in SAM, preventing effective license management and compliance tracking for those products.

questions.stem: Does Performance Analytics (PA) come with Software Asset Management Professional?

options.text: Only if Orchestration has also been licensed
Yes, but if you want to use it for other than SAM it requires additional licensing
No, you must license it separately

questions.explanation: Yes, full Performance Analytics comes with SAM Professional. SAM Professional includes PA as part of its application, providing dashboards, indicators, and trend analysis for software compliance, usage, and optimization metrics. questions.explanation: The Content Service must be opted in to and can be opted out of in the future if required. It is not automatically enabled — organizations must explicitly enable it through the Content Service setup page. Once enabled, it can be disabled later if needed. This gives organizations control over their data sharing with ServiceNow's central content library.

questions.stem: Which is an invalid removal justification when reviewing potential Removal candidates on the License usage view?
questions.explanation: Duplicate License is an invalid removal justification when reviewing Removal Candidates on the License usage view. Valid removal justifications include Low Usage (A), Restricted Software (B), Unallocated (C), and Unlicensed (E). Duplicate licenses are handled through entitlement management, not software removal.
